items.headline: LeBron James Signs with Philadelphia 76ers in Shocking 'Last Decision'
items.summary: NBA legend LeBron James has officially signed a two-year, $8 million veteran's minimum contract with the Philadelphia 76ers, ending speculation about his future. James, who previously considered retirement, announced his move on social media, calling it his 'last decision' and expressing his desire to energize a new fanbase and pursue another championship in what will be his 24th season.

items.headline: Lakers Land Walker Kessler in Key Sign-and-Trade Deal
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers have made a significant offseason move, acquiring center Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz via a sign-and-trade. A Lakers executive highlighted Kessler's ability to be a defensive anchor, providing crucial rim protection and rebounding, while also hinting at his offensive potential.

items.headline: Thunder's Holmgren Reflects on Offseason Roster Shake-Up
items.summary: OKC Thunder big man Chet Holmgren has shared his thoughts on the team's offseason, which saw them part ways with key role players like Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins, and Isaiah Joe. These moves were reportedly made to manage the team's luxury tax obligations without disrupting the core roster.

items.headline: Zach LaVine Expected to Remain with Kings After Buyout Talks Conclude
items.summary: After weeks of speculation, Zach LaVine is reportedly set to remain with the Sacramento Kings, as discussions regarding a potential contract buyout have concluded without a deal.

items.headline: LeBron James' Contract Details with Philadelphia Emerge
items.summary: LeBron James' surprising move to the Philadelphia 76ers will see him sign a two-year contract worth $8 million, taking the veteran's minimum. This comes after earning nearly $53 million last season and reflects his stated motivation to compete for a championship rather than financial gain.

items.headline: Spurs Conclude Summer League with Strong 4-1 Record
items.summary: The San Antonio Spurs wrapped up their 2026 NBA Summer League campaign on a high note, finishing with an impressive 4-1 record. The young core showcased strong performances, building momentum heading into the offseason.

items.headline: Bulls' Caleb Wilson Shines as Summer League Standout
items.summary: Chicago Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson emerged as a top performer during the 2026 NBA Summer League. He was the fifth leading scorer overall and the highest scorer among players who participated in at least four games, highlighted by a dominant 35-point debut that included seven three-pointers.

items.headline: Offseason Coaching Carousel Continues Across the NBA
items.summary: Several teams have finalized their coaching staffs this offseason. Tiago Splitter has taken the helm as Head Coach for the Chicago Bulls, Dusty May is leading the Dallas Mavericks, Sean Sweeney is now with the Orlando Magic, Jamahl Mosley with the New Orleans Pelicans, and Micah Nori with the Portland Trail Blazers. Additionally, veteran coach Dave Joerger has joined the Denver Nuggets as their lead assistant.

items.headline: Terry Rozier Seeks Dismissal of Gambling Charges
items.summary: NBA veteran Terry Rozier has filed a motion to dismiss two of the four charges he faces in an alleged sports gambling scheme. His attorney argues that evidence, including a text message from a co-conspirator, indicates Rozier did not agree to manipulate his performance or know that bets were being placed on his statistics.

items.headline: Cavaliers Star Donovan Mitchell Reportedly Marries Coco Jones
items.summary: Cleveland Cavaliers guard Donovan Mitchell reportedly tied the knot with Grammy-winning singer and actress Coco Jones on August 1, 2026. The couple has become a prominent power duo in the sports and entertainment worlds.
